problem: LLM-based VLN agents make a single-shot action decision from noisy textualized panoramic observations, with no mechanism to check or correct it. Local mismatches and imperfect reasoning therefore accumulate errors, and many such agents also depend on costly closed-source LLMs.
motivation: Humans consider several possible futures and verify them before acting, whereas a deterministic LLM agent can confidently commit to a locally plausible but wrong view. The paper therefore generates diverse candidate actions and verifies them against the instruction, history and observations before execution, borrowing the self-verification idea from LLM reasoning.
key_idea: Fine-tune LLaMA-2-7B to emit a Prediction-View Match-Action chain-of-thought, sample multiple candidate actions, then re-rank them by counting successes of True-False Verification and Masked-Entity Verification.
insight: The ablation on the R2R val-unseen subset shows that sampling plus majority vote gives only marginal gains (SR 39->40), while adding TFV or MEV gives 42 and 44 SR, and both together give 52 SR / 47 SPL. TFV and MEV are therefore complementary: TFV checks global consistency and MEV checks entity-level grounding. Gains saturate at K=4 candidates and P=4 verification trials, so a moderate inference budget captures most of the benefit.
method: Textual observation: BLIP captions each navigable view, and its heading/elevation is mapped to one of six direction phrases (turn left, go forward, go up, etc.). The two are concatenated and labelled A, B, C... as action options.
Navigational CoT: the LLM outputs Prediction (next expected landmark), View match (which option supports it) and Action (chosen option), guided by one in-context example.

CoT ground-truth collection: an LLM extracts entities from the instruction, and CLIP picks the entity most similar to the ground-truth next-view image as the Prediction label. The View match and Action labels are the GT action option.

In-domain training: LLaMA-2-7B with bias tuning (about 1.6M trainable parameters). Stage 1 is multi-task pretraining on separate Pred/VM/Act losses; stage 2 is finetuning on full CoT sequences from expert trajectories.
Sampling decoding: K candidate CoT-conditioned actions are sampled per step. If all candidates agree, the action is executed directly and verification is skipped.
True-False Verification: the verifier LLM is asked P times whether the candidate is the correct next step given the instruction, history and observations. The score is the count of True answers.

Masked-Entity Verification: R key instruction entities are masked one at a time, and the verifier tries P times to recover each one assuming the candidate action is taken. The score is the count of correct reconstructions.
Selection: S = S_TFV + S_MEV and argmax over candidates. Ties are broken by higher TFV score, then by earliest decoding order.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-2-7B (bias-tuned, fine-tuned) as navigator and verifier, with BLIP captioner and CLIP for label construction
setting.training_data: In-domain VLN trajectories of the benchmark (R2R, RxR English, REVERIE) with constructed step-wise CoT labels; no extra synthetic or cross-modal pretraining data
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB converted to text (BLIP captions + direction phrases); the LLM sees only text
setting.action_space: Discrete navigable viewpoint options (letters) plus stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (CLIP/GT-based CoT labels are used only for training)

numbers.extra: K=4 samples, P=4 verifications; no extra pretraining data

results: On R2R val-unseen DV-VLN reaches 52 SR / 45 SPL, beating the best prompting baseline MSNav (46/40) and the language-only NavCoT (40/37). It is still well below cross-modal ScaleVLN (81/70) and other language-only agents such as EvolveNav (71/63). On RxR-English it gets 29.16 SR, above NavCoT (24.52), and on REVERIE 29.8 SR, above NavGPT (19.2) and HAMT (23.8).
limitations: The vision-to-text pipeline loses fine-grained visual cues, and the approach remains far below cross-modal and high-resource LLM agents (e.g. ScaleVLN, EvolveNav, NavGPT-2) on R2R.
Repeated sampling and verification add inference latency and compute.
Ablations and sensitivity analyses use only a small 90-episode R2R val-unseen subset, and MEV depends on English-only CLIP-style alignment, so RxR is evaluated on the English subset only.
